blocking.title: G10 still passes when README.md and docs/REPORT.md embed a hand-edited figure as an HTML img tag, a titled Markdown image, an image whose alt text has brackets, or a reference-style image
blocking.evidence: IMAGE_RE is r"!\[[^\]]*\]\(([^)\s]+)\)". It matches only an inline image with no title and no bracket in its alt text, so stale_parts never sees the other ways CommonMark and GitHub embed an image. Reproduced in a scratch clone of af5ddc6: copied docs/figures/pilot.svg to docs/img/pilot-copy.svg, changed the three 'Rule broken, : 2' titles to 0 and zeroed the three bars, then embedded the copy in README.md (above '## Status') as and as ![Pilot, per family](docs/img/pilot-copy.svg "Pilot"), and in docs/REPORT.md (above section 6) in those two forms plus ![Pilot [copy]](img/pilot-copy.svg) and ![Pilot copy][pc] with [pc]: img/pilot-copy.svg, and committed. Running the clone's own code gave CLAIMCHECK: PASS 162 claim(s) in 2 document(s), FRESHNESS: PASS 4 derivation(s), 125 live claim(s), and REPORT: CURRENT (rc 0). gate_g10 (tools/ship_check.py) runs exactly claimcheck, freshness, and report-check, so G10 passes while both documents show a figure with fabricated violation counts, and rule 1 covers figures. Control: adding the plain ![plain](img/pilot-copy.svg) gives 'REPORT: STALE ... embeds an image that make report does not generate', so the gap is the syntax. docs/ARTIFACTS.md:84 and D-054 say every image the two documents embed is checked, 'wherever it is kept'. This is the class of the previous B3 with new evidence: the new test (tests/test_report.py test_check_flags_images_the_build_does_not_generate) covers only the plain inline form. Fix: find images with a CommonMark parser (titles, angle-bracket destinations, nested brackets, reference definitions) and also HTML img and source srcset, or fail on any reference in either document to an image file the build does not write, with a mutation test for each form.

blocking.title: The release commit ships half-life-bench without the canary string rule 9 requires, and the plan makes the repository public before one lands
blocking.file: README.md:3, README.md:22, README.md:29; STATUS.md:73 and STATUS.md Needs Raj item 2; src/halflife/bench/templates/ (30 files)
blocking.evidence: Rule 9 (section 9 of the brief): 'Add a canary string to any dataset meant for release.' README.md:3 says the project 'ships a benchmark', and README.md:22 calls this commit 'a release before the main study'. None of the 30 template files under src/halflife/bench/templates/ has a canary (grep -ri canary src/halflife/bench/ finds nothing), as README.md:29 and STATUS.md:73 say. STATUS.md:73 says the templates are to be published, notes that rule 9 asks for a canary, and schedules one for 'before E1'. STATUS.md Needs Raj item 2 asks Raj to make the repository public once CI passes, which comes before E1. So the release plan would publish every template under MIT with no canary, including the held-out E4 templates and their decision points, before E2 and E4 have run. README.md:29 rests on reading a public repository as not a dataset release because the bench is 'not yet packaged as a dataset release'. No DECISIONS.md entry records that reading (grep -i canary DECISIONS.md finds nothing), although rule 10 asks for interpretations to be recorded before acting on them. Fix: add the canary before the repository goes public, with the recorded decision and re-banked template hashes the backlog item describes. Otherwise, record in DECISIONS.md and STATUS.md that the repository stays private until the canary lands, and change README.md:22.

blocking.title: README.md:3 says the project ships 'a preregistered analysis', but no preregistration exists
blocking.evidence: The README's first paragraph says: 'It ships a benchmark, a sandboxed harness, validated detectors, a preregistered analysis, and a mitigation kit for Claude Code'. At af5ddc6, prereg/ holds only .gitkeep (git ls-files prereg/). The same page says 'G11 preregistration integrity (trivially: no preregistration is committed yet)' (README.md:26) and calls the analysis 'to be frozen by a preregistration before the main study runs' (README.md:49). Rule 2 says 'Anything not preregistered is labeled exploratory'. The first screen of the release labels an analysis that has not been preregistered as preregistered. D-052 set out to remove exactly this class ('design files, docstrings, and the report spoke of preregistrations in the present tense, though none is committed yet') but missed this sentence, which dates from 5bf72f8. Fix: say 'an analysis to be preregistered before the main study', and log the change in CORRECTIONS.md, since the claim has been in every README since 5bf72f8.

G11 trusts each artifact's self-declared 'confirmatory' flag (src/halflife/integrity/prereg.py:256-260), and G8/G9 (tools/ship_check.py:1476-1648) never require a preregistration link for E3/E4 even though designs/e3.yaml and designs/e4.yaml declare confirmatory: true. The run tool refuses confirmatory plans without --prereg (src/halflife/experiment.py:543-553), so this is defense in depth; consider deriving confirmatory status from the committed design.

Probes advance the main run's seed counter (src/halflife/agent.py:258-260, temperature 0.7), so main-run sampling depends on how many probes ran. Probe content never enters the main context, and probes run in every E1 condition, so there is no bias between arms, but 'never contaminate the main run' holds for content only; say so, or give probes their own seed stream.
G5 probe leakage is recomputed only from per-session leak flags the harness wrote (src/halflife/experiment.py:445). Main-run contexts are not banked, so leakage cannot be re-derived from artifacts/.
